normalized.description: New (stricter) approaches to space debris generation and mitigation are currently being developed that are likely to have cost and operational impacts on telecommunication missions: either in the near term, by voluntary application, or in the longer term, as a condition for launch authorisation or granting market access. Considerations such as an expansion of the protected orbital regions, improved end-of-life disposal rates, better on-station health monitoring, shorter orbital clearance times, and mandatory energy passivation, are all being considered as part of a move toward a Zero-Debris' philosophy for future missions. The first objective of thisstudy is therefore to assess the impacts that applying such an approach would have within the commercial satcom sector. Initial recommendations have not been specifically aimed at the commercial market, so the second objective of the study is to generate commercial-satcom-specific recommendations, considering competitiveness and large-scale constellation operations from the outset.
